headline: NYU Langone researchers have built an AI model that combines heart tracings and blood tests to spot transplant rejection, possibly sparing some patients a biopsy.
score_reason: Early single-center study with a 38-patient test group; published 25 Sep (older than 6 Oct); lowered by 1.
importance_line: Heart transplant recipients who now face repeated biopsies could benefit later, but the result comes from one center's small test group and needs larger confirmation.
summary: News-Medical, as relayed by UA.News, reports that NYU Langone Health researchers trained AI models on ECG and blood-test data to detect heart transplant rejection, and in a 38-patient test group the combined model correctly identified 94% of patients with no rejection. The study, published on 25 Sep 2026 in JHLT Open, is early, and the authors plan larger tests at several transplant centers.
notes: Pool credited Medical Xpress; that page was blocked, so the entry rests on the UA.News relay of News-Medical.
